batch_note: No letter or position pattern: the keys run 10/10/10/10 and agree with my cold answers on all 40. Two template patterns ACROSS items: (1) Every passage uses the same build: one planted lure detail per distractor, each followed by a fact that refutes it. Distractors usually get a surface word in the passage (corridor/strip in A-02, canteen/shrimp feeding in A-03, churned/flood in A-04, roundup/ponies in B-06, receipt/seal in B-05, encrusted/barnacles in C-02, firebreak/fire in C-03, depository/storage in C-04, magnet/visitors in D-04, stained/orange in E-03, thermometer/hot 1860s in E-04, strongbox/sealed holds in E-07, vault/chests in E-08). The key's own word is almost never echoed. A solver who learns 'the option the passage names is a trap' could beat several items without reasoning. This is a hypothesis to attack, not a measurement. (2) Ten items use the frame 'a study/report/survey concluded that [natural agent] had ___ the [place/thing]', with a transitive verb for an environmental effect (A-04, C-02, C-05, C-06, C-08, D-01, D-07, E-02, E-03, E-06). C-02 and D-07 are near-twin worlds: a slate-laden wooden ship sunk off a sandy coast, two centuries on the seabed, one exposed (gnawed) and one buried (interred). Seeing both in one form would cue the contrast. The options in each sub-batch alliterate (A c/b, B p/r, C d/e/f/g, D i/j/l/m/n, E s/t/w). That is a construction constraint and does not point to the key.
